text:
alex: FYI CS flagged Acme seeing a spike of 503s starting ~09:12 UTC. They report short lived but frequent failures during long prompts.

cs_lead: Got a few customer screenshots, all 503 gateway errors. They said the requests are usually ~120k tokens context (long).

alex: I pulled the last 20 logs for their tenant id. Upstream shows repeated worker exit + container restart. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] ERROR infer-runner: worker pid=2145 exited code=139 (segfault)
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] ERROR nvml: GPU 0: out of memory while allocating 1.2GiB for KV cache
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] INFO container: respawned worker (id=2146)
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] WARN gateway: upstream returned 500, routing fallback
```

support-bot: Incident alert posted: hosted-infer-503s-acme-8570000000. Pager duty notified to oncall.

emma: Can we tell whether this is a pure OOM or a kernel fault from the coredump? I grabbed /var/crash/core. gdb shows: 
```
#0  0x00007f8a ... __memcpy_sse2_unaligned
#1  0x0000555f ... kv_cache::prefetch(..)
#2  0x0000555f ... attention_kernel::execute
#3  0x0000555f ... runner::handle_request
```

jamal: Looks like a KV prefetch memcpy into an oversized allocation. Combined with the nvml OOM lines, my guess: prefetch attempted to reserve >available GPU mem on large context and then corrupts memory if allocation fails fast-path. Repro: send a single request with context_size=120000 tokens + toolcall attached.

tess: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Route Acme to fallback smaller model variant (they're on hosted v2-large) 2) Apply temporary request-size limiter per-tenant (reject >64k tokens) 3) Disable KV-prefetch for affected pool (hotfix toggle). What do we want to do now?

alex: CS wants minimal customer disruption — prefer routing to fallback model variant. Can infra flip routing for tenant acme-tenant-42 to v2-medium?

jamal: Yes. I can add a rule: if tenant==acme-tenant-42 -> model=v2-medium for 30m. Doing it now. patch: 
```
PATCH /routing/policies/tenant-overrides
{ "tenant": "acme-tenant-42", "model": "v2-medium", "ttl": 1800 }
```

support-bot: Routing policy committed by jamal at 09:18 UTC.

alex: CS pinged: customer reports traffic improved but one residual 503 in the last 10m. They want a writeback on cause and ETA for permanent fix.

tess: For a permanent fix we should: - add allocation guard in kv-prefetch to fall back to on-device chunking instead of a single big allocation - add a per-request pre-check for available GPU mem - add retry/backoff in runner to avoid immediate segfault/abort. I'll file a ticket and prioritize high.

jamal: Repro steps I used: 
1) curl -X POST /v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <acme-key>" -d '{"model":"v2-large","context_size":120000,"prompt":"<big>"}'
2) Observe worker exit in logs 1-2s after request
3) gcore shows memory corruption on heap near kv buffer

emma: Saving core and nvml logs to /srv/forensics/acme/8570000000/; attaching to ticket. Also grabbed GPU usage graph — memory steadily climbs then spike to >98% at crash.

cs_lead: I'll send a customer update: "We've routed your traffic to a stable variant to stop interruptions and are actively fixing the prefetch path that caused out-of-memory segfaults. We'll follow up with an RCA and ETA within 48 hours." Anyone want to review before I send?

alex: LGTM. Add note that we recommend customers avoid >64k token contexts for now.

jamal: I'll follow up with a hotfix proposal and a PR later today to add a pre-check and a defensive allocation path.

tess: Oncall acked. Marking incident as "mitigated" for now; will reopen if we see new crashes. :thumbsup: 

support-bot: Incident mitigated at 09:23 UTC. Metrics stable (p95 503s down to baseline)

cs_lead: Thanks everyone — will update Acme and close the loop once PR lands and we have a deploy window.

alex: Quick follow-up: add an alert for sudden GPU mem >90% + segfaults in same 30s window. We should detect this pattern earlier.

jamal: on it. I will add an aggregator rule to the metrics teamboard and link to the incident.

emma: saving timeline and artifacts to ticket INC-2026-857 and uploading to internal drive.

cs_lead: closing thread, moving to postmortem once RCA written."
